description:
You have a Maven Java project 'tuple-utils' open in IntelliJ IDEA, located at /home/ga/IdeaProjects/tuple-utils. It contains 5 Java source files in the package org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple (under src/main/java/):

- Pair.java — Abstract base class for a generic pair of two elements
- ImmutablePair.java — Immutable (thread-safe) pair implementation
- MutablePair.java — Mutable pair implementation
- Triple.java — Abstract base class for a generic triple of three elements
- ImmutableTriple.java — Immutable (thread-safe) triple implementation

These files contain working Java code but have NO Javadoc documentation at all. Your task is to:

1. Read and understand each source file
2. Add class-level Javadoc to every public/abstract class, including:
   - A description of the class purpose
   - @param tags for type parameters (e.g., @param <L> the left element type)
3. Add method-level Javadoc to every public and protected method, including:
   - A description of what the method does
   - @param tag for each parameter
   - @return tag for non-void methods
   - @throws tag where exceptions can be thrown
4. Ensure all Javadoc descriptions are meaningful (not placeholder text)
5. Make sure the project still compiles after your changes (run 'mvn compile')
6. Generate HTML documentation by running: 'mvn javadoc:javadoc'
   The HTML output should appear at target/site/apidocs/
7. Create a summary file at /home/ga/IdeaProjects/tuple-utils/doc-report.txt containing a count of how many classes and methods you documented

All Javadoc should follow standard Java documentation conventions. The descriptions should accurately describe what the code does based on your reading of the implementation.
